title: CReal.ivt_bisect_cauchy: the named bisection points, under a uniformly positive derivative, form a genuine Cauchy sequence
statement: Under the same hypotheses as CReal.ivt_bisect_cauchy_bound -- uniform continuity AND a uniformly positive derivative bounded away from zero by 1/(k+1) -- CReal.ivt_bisect_cauchy concludes CReal.Cauchy of the sequence `e |-> CReal.ivt_bisect_hi F a b (Nat.succ (Nat.mul 2 e)) K`. This is the point at which the bisection sequence becomes something CReal's convergence machinery (CReal.converges_of_cauchy and its neighbours) can act on directly, which a sequence of CReal.ivt_approx's existential witnesses never could -- `forall e, exists x, ...` does not eliminate into a Type. It states nothing about the sequence's limit being a root of F -- that is CReal.ivt_exact_root, built on top of this fact together with CReal.converges_comp_eventually and CReal.equiv_zero_of_small.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.ivt_bisect_cauchy : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal) -> ((x4 : CReal.HasDerivativeOn x0 x1 x2 x3) -> ((x5 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x2 x3) -> ((x6 : CReal.le x2 x3) -> ((x7 : CReal.le (x0 x2) CReal.zero) -> ((x8 : CReal.le CReal.zero (x0 x3)) -> ((x9 : AxNat) -> ((x10 : ((x10 : CReal) -> ((x11 : CReal.le x2 x10) -> ((x12 : CReal.le x10 x3) -> CReal.le (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x9)) (x1 x10))))) -> CReal.Cauchy (fun (x11 : AxNat) => CReal.ivt_bisect_hi x0 x2 x3 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x11)) (AxNat.add (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (CReal.bound (CReal.add x3 (CReal.neg x2)))) (CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn.modulus x0 x2 x3 x5 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x11)))) (CReal.bound (CReal.add x3 (CReal.neg x2))))))))))))))))
